_description: Expected JSONL entity shape produced by the pyatlan_v9 asset-mapper (.creator()) pattern. Structural guard rail — relationship refs live under relationshipAttributes, not nested inside attributes; tenantId/status are not duplicated at the top level (status is top-level, tenantId is attributes-only).
_note: sdk_injected_attributes are added by the SDK framework (not app mappers) — connectionName, lastSync*

table._note: All four table_only_attributes are set together in the same 'if isinstance(asset, Table)' branch in map_table — equally exclusive to Table, not just rowCount/subType. This is a documentation cross-reference (what the sibling 'view' spec entry can never have), not an independent check; required_attributes above is what assert_structure() actually validates.

view._note: 'definition' is genuinely View-only on the pyatlan_v9 model — Table has no such field at all (AttributeError on assignment). 'description' is NOT model-restricted (Database/Schema/Table/Column/Procedure all have it too) and is populated on Table/View/Column/Procedure alike from each's *_COMMENT column (aliased 'remarks' by the extract_*.sql files). Database/Schema stay unset — not a gap in this connector, but a real MySQL limitation: the catalog level ('def') isn't a real object (a JDBC-driver placeholder), and standard MySQL has no schema/database-level comment concept at all (information_schema.SCHEMATA has no comment column; CREATE DATABASE has no COMMENT clause — that's a MariaDB-only extension, not applicable to this connector's standard-MySQL queries). 'isPartitioned'/'partitionCount' are Table-only on the model (View lacks them entirely) — unlike the legacy hand-rolled shape, which set them unconditionally on both.
